To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ion exchange process can be successfully used to produce HAs with a high purity and the electrodialysis based regeneration of the spent ion exchange resins is feasible

a process combination consisting of an ion exchange step and an electrodialysis based process step enables the efficient recovery and purification of HAs from alkaline BLs and the regeneration of ion exchange resins with a simultaneous generation of Na2SO4 and NaOH.
ion exchange with SAC resins can be used to efficiently convert the Na+ ions in soda BL and thiosulfates free kraft BL into H2SO4.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new process concept for the efficient production of HAs from secondary sources and the simultaneous chemical recycling of spent resins.
the development of a new process combination of ion-exchange and electrodialyis for the recovery and purifcation of hydroxy acids, such as 2,3-butanedione-2-monoxime (BDM), from secondary sources.

the development of a process combination of electrodialysis (ED) and ion exchange (IE) for the recovery and separation of hydroxy acids and other valuable components from secondary sources, i.e. black liquors (soda and kraft) from pulp mills.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of ion exchange, electrodialysis, and bipolar membranes can provide a closed loop process for the production of HAs and the regeneration of the ion exchange resin.
the combination of ion exchange with SAC and electrodialyses with bipolar membranes is a promising process for the recovery and production of HAs from BLs.

the combination of ion exchange with strong anion exchange and cation exchange resins and electrodialytic generation of sulfuric acid and sodium hydroxides from spent regenerants is a promising and feasible process for the recovery and recycling of hydroxy acids.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combination of ion exchange with electrodialysis with a bipolar membrane (EDBM) can be used for the recovery of hydroxy acids.

the combination of ion exchange with strong acid cation and strong base anion exchange resin and bipolar membrane electrodialysis can be a very promising process combination for the production of HAs from alkaline BLs and the efficient chemical recycling of the spent resins.
the combination of ion exchange with SAC and EDBM can be used for the recovery and production of HAs and the generation of NaOH and sulfuric acid from spent resin regenerants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the process combination of ion-exchange and electrodialytic regeneration of the SAC resins can be used to produce high-purity HAs from secondary sources with low chemical and energy consumption.
a process combination with ion exchange and EDBM can be used to recover HAs in the form of free acids from alkaline soda or kraft BL based mixtures of sodium salts.
the combination of ion exchange with SAC resin and EDBM can be used to recover hydroxy acids from black liquor and generate sodium hydroxide as a byproduct.
